questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles async tasks, locks held across awaits, or cancellation? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A dispatch task is aborted by shutdown while it is awaiting the driver's answer to an offer. What state is that driver left in?
choices: Offered for the ride, forever, because the abort skipped the cleanup code
Available again, because dropping the future drops the Reservation, which releases the driver
OnTrip, because the offer was already sent
Offered until the driver sends their next location update, which resets the state

questions.prompt: Why can DriverPool safely use std::sync::Mutex in code running on a tokio runtime?
choices: tokio replaces std mutexes with async ones at compile time
unwrap on lock() makes the guard Send across tasks
The HashMap inside is lock-free, so the Mutex is never contended
Critical sections are short, synchronous, and never contain an .await, so the guard is never held while the task is suspended

questions.prompt: Thousands of ride requests arrive in a burst. How does Dispatcher::run limit the load on the driver gateway?
choices: It takes a semaphore permit before receiving the next request, so at most max_in_flight dispatches run and the rest wait in the channel
It spawns a task per request but each task waits for a free driver before calling the gateway
It drops requests that arrive while max_in_flight dispatches are running
It relies on OFFER_TIMEOUT to cancel the extra tasks
